entries.name: Hair clipper
entries.definition: An electric device with a moving blade that is used to cut or trim hair, common in barbering.

entries.name: HAMMER file system
entries.definition: A file system created for the DragonFly BSD operating system, with snapshots and fine-grained history.

entries.name: Hammer.js
entries.definition: A JavaScript library that recognises touch gestures such as swipe, pinch and rotate in web pages.

entries.name: Hand lettering
entries.definition: Drawing letters by hand as decorative artwork, rather than typing them or using a typeface.

entries.name: Hand therapy
entries.definition: Rehabilitating injuries and conditions of the hand, wrist and arm, usually as an occupational or physical therapist.

entries.name: Handle System
entries.definition: A system for assigning, managing and resolving persistent identifiers for digital objects, specified in IETF RFCs and run by CNRI.

entries.name: Handlebars.js
entries.definition: A JavaScript templating library that builds HTML from templates with placeholders for data.

entries.name: hapi
entries.definition: A Node.js framework for building web applications and services, with configuration-driven routing and plugins.

entries.name: Hardware configuration management
entries.definition: Tracking and controlling the versions, settings and changes of hardware components and systems.

entries.name: HashiStack
entries.definition: An informal name for the group of HashiCorp infrastructure tools, such as Terraform, Vault, Consul and Nomad.

entries.name: Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points
entries.definition: A systematic, preventive approach to food safety that finds hazards and sets controls at the critical points where they can be prevented or removed.

entries.name: Hazardous material containment and control
entries.definition: Preventing and containing releases of hazardous materials and controlling people's exposure to them.

entries.name: Hazardous material handling
entries.definition: Storing, moving and using hazardous materials safely and in line with the rules for them.

entries.name: HCFA regulations
entries.definition: Medicare and Medicaid rules issued by the US Health Care Financing Administration, which was renamed the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services in 2001.

entries.name: Head-mounted display
entries.definition: A display worn on the head, such as a virtual or augmented reality headset, that places images in front of the user's eyes.

entries.name: Health and wellness coaching
entries.definition: Guiding clients to set and reach health and lifestyle goals through structured conversations and support for behaviour change.

entries.name: Health economics and outcomes research
entries.definition: The field that applies economic and outcomes-measurement methods to judge the value, cost and effects of health care interventions.

entries.name: Health, safety and environment
entries.definition: The field concerned with protecting people and the environment from workplace hazards and with meeting the related legal requirements.

entries.name: Healthcare delivery science
entries.definition: The study of how health care services are organised, delivered and improved to raise quality, access and value.

entries.name: Healthcare Effectiveness Data and Information Set
entries.definition: A set of standardised measures of health plan performance, maintained by the National Committee for Quality Assurance.

entries.name: Healthcare facilities planning
entries.definition: Planning the space, equipment and services of hospitals and other health care buildings.

entries.name: Healthcare industry knowledge
entries.definition: Understanding of how the health care sector works, including its providers, payers, regulation and terminology.

entries.name: Healthcare quality
entries.definition: The study and practice of measuring and improving the safety, effectiveness and patient focus of health care services.

entries.name: Healthcare strategy
entries.definition: Setting long-term goals and plans for a health care organisation, such as its services, markets and partnerships.

entries.name: Hearing aid software
entries.definition: Software used to fit, program and adjust hearing aids to a person's hearing loss.

entries.name: Heat bending of wood
entries.definition: Shaping wood into curves by softening it with heat or steam and bending it around a form.

entries.name: Heatmap
entries.definition: A data visualisation that shows the size of values as colours across a grid or an area.

entries.name: Heavy equipment operation
entries.definition: Operating large construction and earthmoving machines such as excavators, bulldozers and loaders.

entries.name: Heavy vehicle operation
entries.definition: Driving large road vehicles such as trucks and buses.

entries.name: Heritrix
entries.definition: An open-source, archival-quality web crawler developed by the Internet Archive.

entries.name: Higher education law
entries.definition: The body of law that governs colleges and universities, including student rights, accreditation, funding and employment.

entries.name: Higher education policy
entries.definition: The study and practice of the public and institutional rules, funding and governance that shape colleges and universities.

entries.name: HincII
entries.definition: A type II restriction enzyme, formerly named HindII, that cuts DNA at a specific six-base recognition sequence.

entries.name: HindIII
entries.definition: A type II restriction enzyme from Haemophilus influenzae that cuts DNA at the sequence AAGCTT.

entries.name: Hindsight bias
entries.definition: The tendency, after an outcome is known, to believe one would have predicted it.

entries.name: Historic preservation
entries.definition: The field of protecting and conserving historic buildings, sites and objects.

entries.name: Historical linguistics
entries.definition: The study of how languages change over time and how they are related to one another.

entries.name: History of education
entries.definition: The study of how education and schooling have developed over time.

entries.name: History of medicine
entries.definition: The study of how medical practice, knowledge and institutions have developed over time.

entries.name: History of philosophy
entries.definition: The study of how philosophical ideas and thinkers have developed over time.
